label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, duplicate-delivery, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. The harness withheld recent_deploys, service_health: each call to it got the error its source gives when it does not answer, and never reached that source (an outage simulated for this case; the stack itself was not touched). Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on step_budget after 10 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: missing-deploys
case.title: Payments counted twice in the books, with docker withheld from the tools
case.right_answer: The ledger consumer books a second time every webhook the provider sends again: its dedupe is gone (fault 1's recorded cause, which a deploy brought). Docker did not answer the two tools that read it, so the deploy list and the containers' health could not be read: a right diagnosis says what it could not check, and claims no deploy it has no evidence for. Rolling the ledger consumer back still fits the remedy: code plans a rollback from the deploy log, not from the tools.
